98094402.s: A long-distance walking track equipped with sports apparatus along its length, popular with all kinds of visitors for exercise or a break from the day. Al Hijra Walkway is one of the first long-distance walking venues in Madinah. It was developed under the Quality of Life Program, part of Saudi Vision 2030, to create a lively environment that supports healthy lifestyles through sport, culture, heritage, arts and entertainment. The walkway has wide, comfortable paths flanked by green lawns and palm trees, full lighting, and parking on both sides, and it is 3 kilometres long.
98094402.b: A long-distance walking track equipped with sports apparatus along its length, popular with all kinds of visitors for exercise or a break from the day. Al Hijra Walkway is one of the first long-distance walking venues in Madinah. It was developed under the Quality of Life Program, part of Saudi Vision 2030, to create a lively environment that supports healthy lifestyles through sport, culture, heritage, arts and entertainment. The walkway has wide, comfortable paths flanked by green lawns and palm trees, full lighting, and parking on both sides, and it is 3 kilometres long. It lies in one of the city's busiest areas for shops and restaurants, and is one of the main open-air retreats for Madinah residents and visitors.

98094379.s: Al Qaswa Walkway is one of Madinah's most important facilities for residents and visitors, a pleasant place to spend time with family and friends and designed for long-distance walking. It lies in the south-west of Madinah in Al Qaswa District, on Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl Street, about 4 kilometres from Quba Mosque. The walkway is named after the district in which it was built, chosen by residents and visitors in a poll run by the Municipality on its website.
98094379.b: Al Qaswa Walkway is one of Madinah's most important facilities for residents and visitors, a pleasant place to spend time with family and friends and designed for long-distance walking. It lies in the south-west of Madinah in Al Qaswa District, on Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl Street, about 4 kilometres from Quba Mosque. The walkway is named after the district in which it was built, chosen by residents and visitors in a poll run by the Municipality on its website. It is one of the newest park projects carried out by the Madinah Municipality as part of its strategic plans to improve quality of life, enliven public parks and expand green cover, and is one of the 17 main walkways spread across the city's districts. The walkway and park together cover 110,000 square metres, with 21,000 square metres of green lawns and dedicated tracks for walking and sport.
98094379.a: Al Qaswa District, Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl Street, South-West Madinah

98094337.s: Al Awsiyah Reserve was established as the first bird reserve in Madinah, adding a scenic new attraction for local people. It is known for its abundance and variety of birds, with more than 300 birds of over 25 different species. The place has a distinctive rural design, suited to outings, tourism and enjoying the scenery. The reserve is a farmed area with a number of palm trees, covered with transparent canopies that let sunlight in and shelter a variety of birds, along with seating areas and hospitality for visitors.
98094337.b: Al Awsiyah Reserve was established as the first bird reserve in Madinah, adding a scenic new attraction for local people. It is known for its abundance and variety of birds, with more than 300 birds of over 25 different species. The place has a distinctive rural design, suited to outings, tourism and enjoying the scenery. The reserve is a farmed area with a number of palm trees, covered with transparent canopies that let sunlight in and shelter a variety of birds, along with seating areas and hospitality for visitors. It offers a special experience of watching the birds, listening to their calls, feeding and watering them, and enjoying the natural atmosphere by sitting and strolling. Entry is for families only, not for individuals.

98094315.s: The Al Safiya Museum and Garden project is a cultural tourism oasis in a unique location just steps from the Prophet's Mosque, where knowledge meets leisure and both body and soul are refreshed. Visitors move between a variety of cultural elements, most notably the Story of Creation Museum, an enriching museum that presents striking narrative scenes. The project aims to bring the fragrance of history back to this land as a cultural and leisure destination with sound economic returns, and to complete the site's development as an integrated cultural and investment complex.
98094315.b: The Al Safiya Museum and Garden project is a cultural tourism oasis in a unique location just steps from the Prophet's Mosque, where knowledge meets leisure and both body and soul are refreshed. Visitors move between a variety of cultural elements, most notably the Story of Creation Museum, an enriching museum that presents striking narrative scenes. The project aims to bring the fragrance of history back to this land as a cultural and leisure destination with sound economic returns, and to complete the site's development as an integrated cultural and investment complex.

98094312.t: Al Maktaba Al Amah (Madinah Public Library)
98094312.s: The Public Library is a cultural landmark founded in 1380 AH in front of the Prophet's Mosque, and later moved to its current site in Al Bahr District. It holds modern and old books across many fields, along with many rare books and manuscripts, in total more than 14,000 manuscript and printed volumes. The Kingdom's government wanted Madinah to be a distinguished centre of learning and culture, so the library was founded as a worldwide reference for religious and cultural sciences, and to preserve the contents of the region's endowed libraries.
98094312.b: The Public Library is a cultural landmark founded in 1380 AH in front of the Prophet's Mosque, and later moved to its current site in Al Bahr District. It holds modern and old books across many fields, along with many rare books and manuscripts, in total more than 14,000 manuscript and printed volumes. The Kingdom's government wanted Madinah to be a distinguished centre of learning and culture, so the library was founded as a worldwide reference for religious and cultural sciences, and to preserve the contents of the region's endowed libraries. The library has several facilities with specialised books arranged by a precise subject catalogue, modern electronic means for searching and reading, and quiet, well-prepared spaces that let visitors make good use of its collections.

98094285.s: The Madinah Research and Studies Center was established on the perpetual charitable endowment of His Royal Highness Prince Abdulmajeed bin Abdulaziz Al Saud, may God have mercy on him, who chaired its board. Successive princes of Madinah then led it, including King Salman bin Abdulaziz, may God protect him, when he was Crown Prince in 1432 AH. In 1436 AH, Prince Faisal bin Salman bin Abdulaziz, Governor of Madinah Region, became chairman of the center's board of trustees.
98094285.b: The Madinah Research and Studies Center was established on the perpetual charitable endowment of His Royal Highness Prince Abdulmajeed bin Abdulaziz Al Saud, may God have mercy on him, who chaired its board. Successive princes of Madinah then led it, including King Salman bin Abdulaziz, may God protect him, when he was Crown Prince in 1432 AH. In 1436 AH, Prince Faisal bin Salman bin Abdulaziz, Governor of Madinah Region, became chairman of the center's board of trustees. The center aims to contribute to studies and research about Madinah, to lead in making information and research about the city available, to develop knowledge of its history and civilisation, and to cooperate productively with local and international research centres, experts and researchers. It lies south of Madinah on King Abdullah bin Abdulaziz Road, about 5.4 kilometres from the Prophet's Mosque.
98094285.a: South Madinah, King Abdullah bin Abdulaziz Road

98094282.s: Madinah Arts Center is a cultural centre devoted to enriching Madinah's art and culture scene, and one of the first centres in the Kingdom specialising in visual arts. It hosts a range of exhibitions, workshops and training courses, and lets young people show their work and join communities that help them grow and create. The center opened in 2018 in support of the art and cultural movement, as Madinah's showcase for rich arts and culture, under the Quality of Life Program, part of Saudi Vision 2030.
98094282.b: Madinah Arts Center is a cultural centre devoted to enriching Madinah's art and culture scene, and one of the first centres in the Kingdom specialising in visual arts. It hosts a range of exhibitions, workshops and training courses, and lets young people show their work and join communities that help them grow and create. The center opened in 2018 in support of the art and cultural movement, as Madinah's showcase for rich arts and culture, under the Quality of Life Program, part of Saudi Vision 2030. It has a simple architectural style, with facades of Madinah stone and uniform white walls set against black marble, decorated on the outside with coloured glass. Its total area is 8,200 square metres, with buildings and multi-purpose halls for workshops and art exhibitions, and it supports artists in both traditional and contemporary arts rooted in the identity of Madinah's community.

98094279.s: The Prophet's Mosque Architecture Museum is one of the most important destinations for visitors to the Prophet's Mosque. Its scholarly material gives visitors a picture of the stages of the mosque's expansion and architecture through history, using visual, written and audio displays, and it is one of the services provided by the Agency of the General Presidency for the Affairs of the Prophet's Mosque. It is located in the southern courtyards of the Prophet's Mosque and covers 2,200 square metres. Specialist guides welcome visitors and present the content in Arabic, Urdu and English, while the visual and written content is shown in 12 languages with audio translation using the latest technology.
98094279.b: The Prophet's Mosque Architecture Museum is one of the most important destinations for visitors to the Prophet's Mosque. Its scholarly material gives visitors a picture of the stages of the mosque's expansion and architecture through history, using visual, written and audio displays, and it is one of the services provided by the Agency of the General Presidency for the Affairs of the Prophet's Mosque. It is located in the southern courtyards of the Prophet's Mosque and covers 2,200 square metres. Specialist guides welcome visitors and present the content in Arabic, Urdu and English, while the visual and written content is shown in 12 languages with audio translation using the latest technology. The museum offers visitors knowledge and cultural enrichment, as they learn the history of the Prophet's Mosque over more than 1,400 years, from its founding in the time of the Prophet (peace be upon him), through the era of the Rightly Guided Caliphs to the Saudi era, and discover its features such as the minbar, the mihrab, the domes and the umbrellas.
98094279.a: Southern Courtyards of the Prophet's Mosque, Madinah

98094236.s: The Hejaz Railway station was built on 90,000 square metres in a distinctive late Islamic architectural style, with 12 buildings serving the railway. It opened in 1326 AH (1908 CE) as one of the main railway stations and the line's terminus, built in the reign of Sultan Abdul Hamid II, so that pilgrims from the Levant, Asia and Anatolia could travel from Damascus to Madinah in 5 days instead of 40. The railway suffered intermittent stoppages during the First World War until it stopped for good in 1921. Inside the station walls stands Al Suqya Mosque, named for its closeness to the Suqya well, from which the Prophet (peace be upon him) performed ablution on his way to the Battle of Badr.
98094236.b: The Hejaz Railway station was built on 90,000 square metres in a distinctive late Islamic architectural style, with 12 buildings serving the railway. It opened in 1326 AH (1908 CE) as one of the main railway stations and the line's terminus, built in the reign of Sultan Abdul Hamid II, so that pilgrims from the Levant, Asia and Anatolia could travel from Damascus to Madinah in 5 days instead of 40. The railway suffered intermittent stoppages during the First World War until it stopped for good in 1921. Inside the station walls stands Al Suqya Mosque, named for its closeness to the Suqya well, from which the Prophet (peace be upon him) performed ablution on his way to the Battle of Badr. The museum was founded in 1419 AH (1998 CE) and opened by Prince Abdulmajeed bin Abdulaziz, may God have mercy on him. It is located in King Abdulaziz Square in Al Anbariyah on Omar ibn Al Khattab Street, about 1,020 metres from the Prophet's Mosque.
98094236.a: King Abdulaziz Square, Al Anbariyah, Omar ibn Al Khattab Street, Madinah

98094214.s: Uhud Martyrs Square is one of the best-known landmarks that Muslims are keen to visit, for its historical link to the Battle of Uhud, fought in the third year after the Hijra. The square lies 5 kilometres north of the Prophet's Mosque and includes several sites: Sayyid Al Shuhada Mosque, built in Rajab 1438 AH; Mount Rumat (the Archers' Hill), a small hill south of Mount Uhud from whose top the square and its landmarks can be seen; Mount Uhud, one of Madinah's largest mountains, after which the battle is named; and the Martyrs' Cemetery, where seventy Companions who died in the battle are buried.
98094214.b: Uhud Martyrs Square is one of the best-known landmarks that Muslims are keen to visit, for its historical link to the Battle of Uhud, fought in the third year after the Hijra. The square lies 5 kilometres north of the Prophet's Mosque and includes several sites: Sayyid Al Shuhada Mosque, built in Rajab 1438 AH; Mount Rumat (the Archers' Hill), a small hill south of Mount Uhud from whose top the square and its landmarks can be seen; Mount Uhud, one of Madinah's largest mountains, after which the battle is named; and the Martyrs' Cemetery, where seventy Companions who died in the battle are buried. At Mount Uhud the Muslims fought the disbelievers of Quraysh. The Prophet (peace be upon him) took shelter there when the battle turned in favour of the polytheists after the archers left their posts. Seventy Muslims were killed, foremost among them Hamza ibn Abdulmuttalib, the Prophet's uncle (peace be upon him), and Mus'ab ibn Umayr, the Muslims' standard-bearer.
98094214.a: North of the Prophet's Mosque, foot of Mount Uhud, Madinah

98094210.s: Uhud Fort was the first protective fort built in Madinah, with two towers for defence and observation. It was built in the late Ottoman period, when the Ottomans feared rebellion against them, on the foot of Mount Uhud for observation and protection. It had openings for firing cannon and others for observation, with an open watch area. Its design is two interlocking round towers, the larger being the main part and the smaller connected to it from inside by a stone staircase leading to the roof.
98094210.b: Uhud Fort was the first protective fort built in Madinah, with two towers for defence and observation. It was built in the late Ottoman period, when the Ottomans feared rebellion against them, on the foot of Mount Uhud for observation and protection. It had openings for firing cannon and others for observation, with an open watch area. Its design is two interlocking round towers, the larger being the main part and the smaller connected to it from inside by a stone staircase leading to the roof. It was built of the mountain's own stone, so its colour blends with the mountain as if it were part of the rock. The fort lies in the north-west of the city, at the north-western end of Mount Uhud, about 9 kilometres from the Prophet's Mosque, and can be reached by Uthman ibn Affan Road, which leads to the north of Madinah.
98094210.a: Uthman ibn Affan Road, North-Western End of Mount Uhud, Madinah

98094209.s: Jabal Bani Ubaid is an important Prophetic landmark and one of the boundaries of the Trench that the Muslims dug around Madinah in the fifth year after the Hijra. That year the Muslims heard that the polytheists of Quraysh and their allies intended to attack Madinah, and Salman the Persian, may Allah be pleased with him, advised the Prophet (peace be upon him) to dig a trench to stop the fighters from entering. The trench ran from Mount Ratij to Jabal Bani Ubaid; the Muhajirun dug from the Ratij side to Dhubab, and the Ansar from Dhubab to Jabal Bani Ubaid.
98094209.b: Jabal Bani Ubaid is an important Prophetic landmark and one of the boundaries of the Trench that the Muslims dug around Madinah in the fifth year after the Hijra. That year the Muslims heard that the polytheists of Quraysh and their allies intended to attack Madinah, and Salman the Persian, may Allah be pleased with him, advised the Prophet (peace be upon him) to dig a trench to stop the fighters from entering. The trench ran from Mount Ratij to Jabal Bani Ubaid; the Muhajirun dug from the Ratij side to Dhubab, and the Ansar from Dhubab to Jabal Bani Ubaid. The site witnessed one of the Prophet's miracles: while digging, the Muslims found a hard rock they could not break, and the Prophet (peace be upon him) struck it three times in succession, giving glad tidings of the conquest of the Levant, Persia and Yemen, and the rock broke apart. The mountain lies north-west of the Prophet's Mosque.
98094209.a: North-West of the Prophet's Mosque, Madinah

98094208.s: The Battle of the Confederates (the Trench) is one of the most famous battles in the Prophet's biography. It took place in Shawwal of the fifth year after the Hijra, when the armies of Quraysh, Ghatafan and their allied tribes, about ten thousand fighters in all, marched on Madinah to destroy the Muslims. The Companion Salman the Persian, may Allah be pleased with him, advised the Prophet (peace be upon him) to dig a trench around the city; he liked the idea and went with his senior Companions to mark out the digging site.
98094208.b: The Battle of the Confederates (the Trench) is one of the most famous battles in the Prophet's biography. It took place in Shawwal of the fifth year after the Hijra, when the armies of Quraysh, Ghatafan and their allied tribes, about ten thousand fighters in all, marched on Madinah to destroy the Muslims. The Companion Salman the Persian, may Allah be pleased with him, advised the Prophet (peace be upon him) to dig a trench around the city; he liked the idea and went with his senior Companions to mark out the digging site. He (peace be upon him) chose the area north-west of the city, known as the lower part of Madinah, because it was salty, marshy ground with few trees, while the other sides of the city were naturally protected by lava fields and dense farms. God Almighty said: "O you who believe, remember the favour of Allah upon you when armies came to you, and We sent upon them a wind and armies you did not see." God turned back the plot of the Confederates with a violent wind that shook their camp, and they withdrew in failure without fighting.
98094208.a: North-West of Madinah, near the Seven Mosques area

98094206.s: Masjid Al-Sajdah is a historic landmark that witnessed a divine glad tiding and a prostration by the Prophet. The Companion Abdulrahman ibn Awf, may Allah be pleased with him, relates: the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) went out until he entered a palm grove and prostrated, and prolonged the prostration until I feared that Allah had taken his soul. I came to look, and he raised his head and asked me why I was worried. He said: "Gabriel, peace be upon him, said to me: Shall I not give you glad tidings? Allah the Almighty says to you: whoever sends blessings upon you, I will send blessings upon him, and whoever greets you with peace, I will greet him with peace." A mosque was then built where the Prophet (peace be upon him) prostrated.
98094206.b: Masjid Al-Sajdah is a historic landmark that witnessed a divine glad tiding and a prostration by the Prophet. The Companion Abdulrahman ibn Awf, may Allah be pleased with him, relates: the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) went out until he entered a palm grove and prostrated, and prolonged the prostration until I feared that Allah had taken his soul. I came to look, and he raised his head and asked me why I was worried. He said: "Gabriel, peace be upon him, said to me: Shall I not give you glad tidings? Allah the Almighty says to you: whoever sends blessings upon you, I will send blessings upon him, and whoever greets you with peace, I will greet him with peace." A mosque was then built where the Prophet (peace be upon him) prostrated. The mosque has great historical importance as one of the Prophetic sites whose location has been preserved to this day, and it also witnessed the descent of Gabriel, peace be upon him, to the Prophet (peace be upon him). Its building was renovated in the Saudi era in 1399 AH, its total area is 1,823 square metres, and it has a minaret at its north-western corner.

98094205.s: Masjid Ali bin Abi Talib stands on the site of one of the Prophet's Eid prayer grounds in the Manakha area, which the Prophet (peace be upon him) used for the Eid prayer and the rain prayer. It is named for Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, who led the people in the Eid al-Adha prayer there during the caliphate of Uthman ibn Affan, may Allah be pleased with him, in 35 AH. It was probably first built in the Umayyad period, when Omar ibn Abdulaziz governed Madinah (87-93 AH), then fell into ruin and disappeared, and was renewed by the Governor of Madinah, Zain al-Din al-Mansouri, in 881 AH.
98094205.b: Masjid Ali bin Abi Talib stands on the site of one of the Prophet's Eid prayer grounds in the Manakha area, which the Prophet (peace be upon him) used for the Eid prayer and the rain prayer. It is named for Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, who led the people in the Eid al-Adha prayer there during the caliphate of Uthman ibn Affan, may Allah be pleased with him, in 35 AH. It was probably first built in the Umayyad period, when Omar ibn Abdulaziz governed Madinah (87-93 AH), then fell into ruin and disappeared, and was renewed by the Governor of Madinah, Zain al-Din al-Mansouri, in 881 AH. The present building dates to the reign of King Fahd bin Abdulaziz, when it was rebuilt and expanded in 1411 AH. It was then restored and preserved in 1434 AH in the reign of King Abdullah bin Abdulaziz, and further maintenance work was carried out in the reign of King Salman bin Abdulaziz as part of the project to care for mosques and historic sites in Madinah.

98092531.s: Masjid Al-Jumua stands where the first Friday prayer in Islam was held. When the Prophet (peace be upon him) migrated from Makkah, he stayed some days in Quba, then set out for Madinah, and the Friday prayer overtook him in a valley near where he was staying; he delivered the sermon and prayed with those who were with him. In the time of Omar ibn Abdulaziz as governor of Madinah, a mosque was built on this spot. It lies about 600 metres from Quba Mosque and about 2,300 metres from the Prophet's Mosque.
98092531.b: Masjid Al-Jumua stands where the first Friday prayer in Islam was held. When the Prophet (peace be upon him) migrated from Makkah, he stayed some days in Quba, then set out for Madinah, and the Friday prayer overtook him in a valley near where he was staying; he delivered the sermon and prayed with those who were with him. In the time of Omar ibn Abdulaziz as governor of Madinah, a mosque was built on this spot. It lies about 600 metres from Quba Mosque and about 2,300 metres from the Prophet's Mosque. It was rebuilt, expanded and equipped with the necessary facilities in the reign of King Fahd bin Abdulaziz in 1412 AH, on 1,630 square metres. It has prayer halls for men and for women that hold 650 worshippers, a slender, elegant minaret, and a main dome in the middle of the prayer hall, along with four smaller domes.
98092531.a: Quba Road to the Prophet's Mosque, Madinah

98092504.s: Masjid Bani Unayf is a historic mosque named for its location among the homes of the Bani Unayf tribe. It dates to the time of the Prophet (peace be upon him): it is reported that he once came to Bani Unayf to visit the Companion Talha ibn al-Bara ibn Umayr, may Allah be pleased with him, a young man of Bani Unayf who was ill, in the second year after the Hijra. During the visit the Prophet (peace be upon him) prayed in their homes near one of their fortresses; Bani Unayf were delighted and kept looking after the place where he prayed, and some time later built a mosque there.
98092504.b: Masjid Bani Unayf is a historic mosque named for its location among the homes of the Bani Unayf tribe. It dates to the time of the Prophet (peace be upon him): it is reported that he once came to Bani Unayf to visit the Companion Talha ibn al-Bara ibn Umayr, may Allah be pleased with him, a young man of Bani Unayf who was ill, in the second year after the Hijra. During the visit the Prophet (peace be upon him) prayed in their homes near one of their fortresses; Bani Unayf were delighted and kept looking after the place where he prayed, and some time later built a mosque there. Historians have mentioned it throughout history, and Ali ibn Musa described it as "a small unroofed mosque". In the Saudi era the mosque received great attention: its old structure was preserved and walls of basalt stone with pointed arches were added to strengthen it, along with a tree-shaded courtyard surrounded by a stone wall that echoes Madinah's traditional architecture.

98092469.s: Masjid Al-Fash is one of Madinah's historic mosques, formerly known as "Masjid Jabal Uhud" because it lies on the mountain's foot, at the entrance of Shi'b Al-Jirar leading to Al-Maharis. It is significant because the Prophet (peace be upon him) prayed on this spot, and because it lies in the area where he took the Muslims for refuge in the final phase of the Battle of Uhud. In Shawwal of the third year after the Hijra, the battle was fought between Mount Uhud and the Archers' Hill; after the archers left their posts the outcome turned, and the Prophet (peace be upon him) withdrew with his Companions to Shi'b Al-Jirar and faced the polytheists until they halted their attack. It was first built in the time of Omar ibn Abdulaziz as governor of Madinah, between 86 and 93 AH in the Umayyad era.
98092469.b: Masjid Al-Fash is one of Madinah's historic mosques, formerly known as "Masjid Jabal Uhud" because it lies on the mountain's foot, at the entrance of Shi'b Al-Jirar leading to Al-Maharis. It is significant because the Prophet (peace be upon him) prayed on this spot, and because it lies in the area where he took the Muslims for refuge in the final phase of the Battle of Uhud. In Shawwal of the third year after the Hijra, the battle was fought between Mount Uhud and the Archers' Hill; after the archers left their posts the outcome turned, and the Prophet (peace be upon him) withdrew with his Companions to Shi'b Al-Jirar and faced the polytheists until they halted their attack. It was first built in the time of Omar ibn Abdulaziz as governor of Madinah, between 86 and 93 AH in the Umayyad era, and it received great attention in the Saudi era.
98092469.a: Foot of Mount Uhud, Entrance of Shi'b Al-Jirar, Madinah

98092468.s: Masjid Al-Miqat (Dhul Hulaifah) is the miqat, the point for entering the state of ihram, for the people of Madinah and those passing through it to perform Hajj and Umrah, and the farthest miqat from Makkah. The Prophet (peace be upon him) used to stop at a tree here to enter ihram, and said: "Tonight someone came to me from my Lord while I was at Al-Aqiq, saying: pray in this blessed valley." Omar ibn Abdulaziz built it of stone, then King Faisal bin Abdulaziz ordered its renewal and expansion, and the major expansion came in the reign of King Fahd bin Abdulaziz, making it a splendid architectural landmark. The mosque lies south-west of Madinah on the western side of Wadi Al-Aqiq, 14 km from the Prophet's Mosque.
98092468.b: Masjid Al-Miqat (Dhul Hulaifah) is the miqat, the point for entering the state of ihram, for the people of Madinah and those passing through it to perform Hajj and Umrah, and the farthest miqat from Makkah. The Prophet (peace be upon him) used to stop at a tree here to enter ihram, and said: "Tonight someone came to me from my Lord while I was at Al-Aqiq, saying: pray in this blessed valley." Omar ibn Abdulaziz built it of stone, then King Faisal bin Abdulaziz ordered its renewal and expansion, and the major expansion came in the reign of King Fahd bin Abdulaziz, making it a splendid architectural landmark. The mosque lies south-west of Madinah on the western side of Wadi Al-Aqiq, 14 km from the Prophet's Mosque. It is square, with a unique geometric design, and has a spiral minaret 62 metres high.

98092464.s: Al Urouba Boulevard is a unique tourist frontage of 10,000 square metres, designed in a modern spirit with green facades and a range of tourist facilities: restaurants, cafes and public spaces for events. The project was built in line with Saudi Vision 2030, under the Quality of Life Program, which aims to improve the quality of life of individuals and families by encouraging participation in cultural, entertainment, sports and tourism activities. It has wide open-air spaces, a variety of entertainment options for families, places to meet and stroll, and a series of modern-style cafes and restaurants. The boulevard is in Al Rayah District and suits all members of the community.
98092464.b: Al Urouba Boulevard is a unique tourist frontage of 10,000 square metres, designed in a modern spirit with green facades and a range of tourist facilities: restaurants, cafes and public spaces for events. The project was built in line with Saudi Vision 2030, under the Quality of Life Program, which aims to improve the quality of life of individuals and families by encouraging participation in cultural, entertainment, sports and tourism activities. It has wide open-air spaces, a variety of entertainment options for families, places to meet and stroll, and a series of modern-style cafes and restaurants. The boulevard is in Al Rayah District and suits all members of the community of every age.

98092456.s: Quba Boulevard is a lively tourist destination with a selection of distinctive restaurants and cafes, offering a pleasant experience of sitting and relaxing, with a variety of food and drinks and a lovely view over Quba Road. It was built as a destination for visitors and local people, with elegant designs and spacious indoor and outdoor seating. Water-mist sprayers throughout keep the air mild and pleasant, making it an ideal place to rest and gather with family. The boulevard is south of Madinah on the southbound Quba Road, about 6.8 kilometres from the Prophet's Mosque and about 3.3 kilometres from Quba Mosque.
98092456.b: Quba Boulevard is a lively tourist destination with a selection of distinctive restaurants and cafes, offering a pleasant experience of sitting and relaxing, with a variety of food and drinks and a lovely view over Quba Road. It was built as a destination for visitors and local people, with elegant designs and spacious indoor and outdoor seating. Water-mist sprayers throughout keep the air mild and pleasant, making it an ideal place to rest and gather with family. The boulevard is south of Madinah on the southbound Quba Road, about 6.8 kilometres from the Prophet's Mosque and about 3.3 kilometres from Quba Mosque.

98092381.s: Al Rashid Mega Mall is one of Madinah's best-known shopping centres, with a variety of local and international shops, game and entertainment halls, and international restaurants. It covers 140,000 square metres over 4 floors, with more than 400 shops and parking for more than 500 cars. Its best-known feature is the artificial lake with an old Arab-style ship at its centre, where visitors sit and take souvenir photos, along with its attractive outdoor squares. The mall is in the east of Madinah on King Abdullah Road (the Second Ring Road) and opens daily from 9 am to 1 am, except Friday, when it opens from 1 pm to 1 am.
98092381.b: Al Rashid Mega Mall is one of Madinah's best-known shopping centres, with a variety of local and international shops, game and entertainment halls, and international restaurants. It covers 140,000 square metres over 4 floors, with more than 400 shops and parking for more than 500 cars. Its best-known feature is the artificial lake with an old Arab-style ship at its centre, where visitors sit and take souvenir photos, along with its attractive outdoor squares. The mall is in the east of Madinah on King Abdullah Road (the Second Ring Road) and opens daily from 9 am to 1 am, except Friday, when it opens from 1 pm to 1 am.
